pr_body:
Fix: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54556

When getting an integer value from the database, all adapters will create return a real integer. But when we initialize an attribute from the column defaults, the attribute is given a string, that's inconsistent.
pr_comments: I believe this change is positive, but I fear it may break existing apps. @matthewd @rafaelfranca any opinions?

@byroot

This PR change is causing a bug in our code when we use `store_accessor` on its own to store attributes in a jsonb column.  eg
```ruby
store_accessor :configuration, %i[ host port ]
```
What's weird is that once a record is created, subsequent instantiations of new records have a cached version of `configuration` set.  This bug disappears if we just call:
```ruby
store :configuration, accessors: %i[ host port ]
```
directly.  I'm still trying to find the exact issue but thought it'd be helpful to flag in case someone else sees as well.
Thanks. Please open a dedicated issue once you have a repro.
@byroot I was able to reproduce here: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54681. Please let me know if there's anything else I can provide.

issue_context.title: ActiveModel attribute with `default` requires to handle a `String` during deserialization
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->
Here's a [gist](https://gist.github.com/Vagab/088bdd5d36e873dd8a13aaab19c9b75c)
```ruby
ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
    t.integer :field, default: 0
  end
end

class FieldType < ActiveModel::Type::Value
  VALUES = { 0 => "zero" }

  def type
    :field_type
  end

  def deserialize(value)
    VALUES.fetch(value) unless value.nil?
  end

  def serialize(value)
    VALUES.key(value)
  end
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  attribute :field, FieldType.new
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_association_stuff
    post = Post.create!

    assert post.field == "zero"
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior

I would expect that the value I receive in `deserialize` is an `Integer`, and the script runs fine

### Actual behavior

The value I receive in `deserialize` is a `String`, and the script fails on `VALUES.fetch`.
As far as I understand this is "intentional", from what I gathered playing with it it seems that all the values that an attribute gets from the db are internally represented as strings. I think I would expect those to be cast to the column type as specified in the database before passed into `deserialize`. But I'm not sure if that's a viable option. In any case I think this is an unexpected behaviour, at least for me, given that it works fine if the column does not have a default.

### System configuration

**Rails version**:
Rails 8.0.1

**Ruby version**: 
ruby 3.3.3 (2024-06-12 revision f1c7b6f435) [arm64-darwin24]
comments:
I dug into this. This only happens when the default is read from the in memory schema cache. The `ActiveRecord::Column#default` is stored as `"0"`. 

We should pass it through the column's type `#deserialize` method before handling it to the attribute type.

review_comments: Would it make sense to deserialize the column default when we build the column instead, so that `Post.columns#default` also returns the deserialized default ?
Possibly, but then we'd have to be careful about mutable values.
